title: Public sentiment and economic uncertainty: an exploratory analysis of Twitter discourse on the anticipated 2023 recession
abstract: Abstract This study analyzes public sentiment surrounding the anticipated 2023 recession by examining 20,000 tweets collected over a 60-day period. Using a set of established natural language processing and machine learning techniques, we classified tweets containing recession-related keywords as positive, negative, or neutral. The results show that negative sentiment dominated the online discussion, reflecting widespread concerns about job security, inflation, and economic instability. Rather than treating social media data as predictive of macroeconomic outcomes, we frame this analysis as an exploratory case study of how economic anxieties are articulated in digital discourse. The findings illustrate both the potential and the limits of sentiment analysis for studying collective mood during periods of uncertainty. While the approach demonstrates how online communities engage with recession narratives, it also underscores challenges of representativeness, temporal scope, and reliance on older NLP models. We conclude that future work should expand to multi-platform data, adopt advanced transformer-based models, and integrate sentiment analysis with other economic and survey indicators. This reframing highlights the methodological value of sentiment analysis in capturing public discourse around crises, providing a foundation for more robust comparative studies.

title: Optoelectronic nonlinear activation with photochromic weighting based on silicon photomultipliers and light-emitting diodes
abstract: The nonlinear response of an artificial optical neuron is a key characteristic that enables neuromorphic computation in optical neural networks. Nonlinear activation functions in optical computing are implemented using either optoelectronic or fully optical approaches. While optical methods can achieve higher operation speeds without added electronic noise, optoelectronic implementations of nonlinear activation provide transfer function tunability, seamless CMOS integration, low optical power operation and realization of electrical and/or optical gain. In this work, a nonlinear activation function is realized using a commercially available silicon photomultiplier (SiPM). The SiPM output current is converted by a transimpedance amplifier (TIA) into a voltage that drives a light-emitting diode (LED) to achieve optical-electrical-optical conversion. Furthermore, weight functions are implemented in the proposed optical system using photochromic materials as entrance windows on the SiPM. Photochromic polymer films are prepared by spin-coating solutions containing dissolved diarylethenes in a polymer matrix. The optical characteristics of the photochromic materials were studied through ultraviolet–visible (UV/Vis) spectroscopy in relation to controlling the absorption properties using two discrete wavelengths in the ultraviolet and visible range. The transfer function of the realized optoelectronic system was measured for different TIA gain, intensity of the input optical power and photochromic material weights. Realization of an XOR function using parallel connection of multiple inputs with integrated weight function to the nonlinear activation function was analyzed through simulations.

title: Smart College Helpdesk Assistant Using Machine Learning & NLP
abstract: The existing higher education helpdesk systems rely on manual processes or a fixed set of frequently asked questions (FAQs) which may result in delays in response, even lost communications and increase in the cost of operations. This study will suggest the development of a Smart College Helpdesk System, which employs advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to provide automated real-time services to students and alleviate these inefficiencies. The presented system architecture uses the Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) model at the level of accurate intent classification and entity recognition, which is a part of an effective Python FastAPI backend and a Streamlit user interface. In contrast to the classical retrieval-based systems, the system embraces multi-turn interactions and is dynamically able to retrieve data in institutional knowledge bases in order to generate context-sensitive answers. Performance tests show that the system can have an average latency of less than one second of automated response even with high volume concurrent user loads. Comparative analysis also proves high accuracy and efficiency as compared to the rule-based alternatives. The created system greatly simplifies the efficiency of the working process and the contentment of students by automating administrative questions and offering 24/7 opportunities, which is a scalable solution to the modern educational system.

abstract: This proposed work presents a novel crowd anomaly detection model comprising four essential stages, namely, preprocessing, object segmentation, feature extraction, and anomaly detection. At first, the input images are preprocessed by using median filtering to improve quality and reduce noise, laying the foundation for subsequent analysis. Object Segmentation employs an Improved Mask R-CNN to accurately delineate objects within the scene, overcoming challenges posed by occlusions and complex backgrounds. Feature Extraction involves extracting discriminative features from segmented objects, including Improved SLBT features, color features, and LGTrP features. These features capture essential characteristics of objects, enabling a more robust representation of the scene. Finally, Anomaly Detection is executed using a hybrid model that combines the efficiency of SqueezeNet and the Improved LinkNet model. This approach uses the strengths of both models to achieve enhanced anomaly detection accuracy. The proposed approach offers a comprehensive solution to the challenges of crowd anomaly detection, promising improved performance and efficiency in real-world scenarios, thereby contributing to advancements in public safety and security.

title: Exploiting Subgradient Sparsity in Max-Plus Neural Networks
abstract: Deep Neural Networks are powerful tools for solving machine learning problems, but their training often involves dense and costly parameter updates. In this work, we use a novel Max-Plus neural architecture in which classical addition and multiplication are replaced with maximum and summation operations respectively. This is a promising architecture in terms of interpretability, but its training is challenging. A particular feature is that this algebraic structure naturally induces sparsity in the subgradients, as only neurons that contribute to the maximum affect the loss. However, standard backpropagation fails to exploit this sparsity, leading to unnecessary computations. In this work, we focus on the minimization of the worst sample loss which transfers this sparsity to the optimization loss. To address this, we propose a sparse subgradient algorithm that explicitly exploits the algebraic sparsity. By tailoring the optimization procedure to the non-smooth nature of Max-Plus models, our method achieves more efficient updates while retaining theoretical guarantees. This highlights a principled path toward bridging algebraic structure and scalable learning.

title: Adaptive integration of model-based and model-free strategies in human reinforcement learning of reachable space
abstract: Most skilled behaviour occurs within reachable space; however, how humans learn to reach around obstacles in this space remains almost entirely unexplored. Here, using a novel robotic maze task that captures the richness of naturalistic hand-object interaction, we show that humans adaptively integrate model-based and model-free reinforcement learning strategies to act in reachable space. Fitting hybrid models to reach trajectories revealed that participants shifted from model-based toward model-free strategies across learning. Specifically, model-free reliance increased with state familiarity and distance from the goal, and with exclusive haptic feedback. Across participants, greater model-free reliance was associated with faster movements, consistent with reduced planning demands. Critically, direct comparison with an analogous virtual navigation task revealed stronger model-free reliance in reachable space than in navigable space, demonstrating that the computational architecture governing spatial learning is shared across scales but calibrated to the costs and constraints of the specific effector system.

title: Physically generated masking sequences with GHz tunability for time delay reservoir computing
abstract: This work investigates the generation of diverse, low-correlation temporal patterns using a long-cavity semiconductor laser with external optical feedback. The system produces tunable, GHz-scale waveforms rich in harmonic content. Pattern diversity is enhanced through spectral electrical or optical shaping. These structured signals are ideal for photonic time delay reservoir computing, where input encoding typically relies on complex digital waveform generators. By offering an analog, self-sustained alternative, this approach simplifies signal generation while maintaining high diversity and repeatability. Experimental results validate earlier theoretical predictions, highlighting the potential of nonlinear laser dynamics in optical information processing.

title: Hybrid Machine Learning Model for Robust Financial Fraud Detection
abstract: The rapid growth of digital financial services such as online banking, card payments and mobile transactions has increased the number of fraudulent activities which makes fraud detection a major challenge for researchers. Traditional fraud detection methods depend on a single machine learning model which often fails to identify unusual transaction patterns, time-based behavior and complex relationships between features at the same time. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a hybrid fraud detection framework that combines unsupervised anomaly detection, temporal deep learning, and ensemble gradient boosting models. First the transaction data are preprocessed, normalized and enhanced by extracting important behavioral and transaction level features along with user based statistical information. An autoencoder is used to detect unusual transactions by measuring reconstruction errors while Bidirectional LSTM model learns sequential transaction patterns over time. Finally, LightGBM and XGBoost are used to classify transactions as fraudulent or normal using the improved features. Experimental results show that the proposed approach achieves high performance with 97% accuracy, 95% precision, 98% recall, 96% F1-score and 99% ROC-AUC value. Compared to existing techniques the proposed framework performs better. Ablation studies show that each part of the model is important proving that the hybrid approach works well for detecting fraud in real world financial systems.

title: Optimal recovery for quantum error correction
abstract: The calculation of the error threshold of quantum error correcting codes typically proceeds as follows. First, syndromes are measured. Then, a decoder infers the error chain and the corresponding correction is applied. The threshold is then defined as the largest correctable error rate, with the maximum-likelihood decoder corresponding to the ``optimal'' threshold. However, a broader set of operations could be used to recover quantum information. The true optimal threshold should be optimised over all possible recovery schemes, which can be described by quantum channels. Here, we study such optimal recovery channels and their thresholds $p_\mathrm{th}^\mathrm{opt}$. We introduce an information-theoretic quantity, mutual trace distance, which provides a necessary and sufficient diagnostic for sharply determining $p_\mathrm{th}^\mathrm{opt}$ without explicit optimisation. In contrast, previous works give a lower bound on $p_\mathrm{th}^\mathrm{opt}$ by specifying particular recovery schemes, e.g. Schumacher-Westmoreland (SW) which provides coherent information as a diagnostic to lower bound $p^\mathrm{opt}_\mathrm{th}$. We prove that the Petz and SW recovery schemes are optimal, i.e. their threshold is $p_\mathrm{th}^\mathrm{opt}$. With their optimality established, we explore the structure of optimal and non-optimal recovery schemes and their phase diagrams.

title: The Empty Quadrant: AI Teammates for Embodied Field Learning
abstract: For four decades, AIED research has rested on what we term the Sedentary Assumption: the unexamined design commitment to a stationary learner seated before a screen. Mobile learning and museum guides have moved learners into physical space, and context-aware systems have delivered location-triggered content -- yet these efforts predominantly cast AI in the role of information-de-livery tool rather than epistemic partner. We map this gap through a 2 x 2 matrix (AI Role x Learning Environment) and identify an undertheorized intersection: the configuration in which AI serves as an epistemic teammate during unstruc-tured, place-bound field inquiry and learning is assessed through trajectory rather than product. To fill it, we propose Field Atlas, a framework grounded in embod-ied, embedded, enactive, and extended (4E) cognition, active inference, and dual coding theory that shifts AIED's guiding metaphor from instruction to sensemak-ing. The architecture pairs volitional photography with immediate voice reflec-tion, constrains AI to Socratic provocation rather than answer delivery, and ap-plies Epistemic Trajectory Modeling (ETM) to represent field learning as a con-tinuous trajectory through conjoined physical-epistemic space. We demonstrate the framework through a museum scenario and argue that the resulting trajecto-ries -- bound to a specific body, place, and time -- constitute process-based evi-dence structurally resistant to AI fabrication, offering a new assessment paradigm and reorienting AIED toward embodied, dialogic human-AI sensemaking in the wild.

title: RVN-Bench: A Benchmark for Reactive Visual Navigation
abstract: Safe visual navigation is critical for indoor mobile robots operating in cluttered environments. Existing benchmarks, however, often neglect collisions or are designed for outdoor scenarios, making them unsuitable for indoor visual navigation. To address this limitation, we introduce the reactive visual navigation benchmark (RVN-Bench), a collision-aware benchmark for indoor mobile robots. In RVN-Bench, an agent must reach sequential goal positions in previously unseen environments using only visual observations and no prior map, while avoiding collisions. Built on the Habitat 2.0 simulator and leveraging high-fidelity HM3D scenes, RVN-Bench provides large-scale, diverse indoor environments, defines a collision-aware navigation task and evaluation metrics, and offers tools for standardized training and benchmarking. RVN-Bench supports both online and offline learning by offering an environment for online reinforcement learning, a trajectory image dataset generator, and tools for producing negative trajectory image datasets that capture collision events. Evaluations demonstrate that policies trained on RVN-Bench generalize effectively across unseen simulated environments. Furthermore, initial physical experiments using a Jackal UGV indicate promising sim-to-real transfer. Code and additional materials are available at: https://sequor-robotics-research.github.io/projects/RVN-Bench/.

title: TRACE: Task-Adaptive Reasoning and Representation Learning for Universal Multimodal Retrieval
abstract: Universal Multimodal Retrieval requires unified embedding models capable of interpreting diverse user intents, ranging from simple keywords to complex compositional instructions. While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) possess strong reasoning capabilities, prevailing adaptations confine them to static encoders, underutilizing their generative potential. This encoder-only paradigm struggles with complex intents that demand logical deduction rather than superficial pattern matching. To address this, we introduce TRACE (Task-adaptive Reasoning And Compressing Embeddings). TRACE unifies generative reasoning with discriminative representation learning. It first generates a structured Chain-of-Thought (CoT) to explicitly reason about the query, and subsequently compresses this reasoning trace into a compact embedding via a dedicated token. To train this framework, we construct M-BEIR-CoT, a large-scale dataset featuring a difficulty-aware routing strategy. Experiments on the M-BEIR benchmark establish TRACE as the new state-of-the-art. Crucially, TRACE demonstrates a learned implicit routing behavior. It autonomously activates reasoning for complex queries while bypassing it for simpler ones, achieving an optimal balance between retrieval accuracy and inference throughput. Furthermore, by internalizing the deductive process, TRACE exhibits remarkable zero-shot transferability to unseen domains and novel constraints.

title: Phân tích tình cảm đa phương thức cho tiếng Việt sử dụng mạng nơ-ron tích chập đồ thị chuẩn hóa
abstract: Phân tích tình cảm đa phương thức (Multimodal Sentiment Analysis - MSA) kết hợp thông tin từ nhiều phương thức, điển hình là văn bản và hình ảnh, nhằm nhận diện chính xác các trạng thái tình cảm của con người. Tuy nhiên, phương pháp MSA hiện nay vẫn gặp hạn chế trong việc mô hình hóa các mối quan hệ cấu trúc ngữ nghĩa phức tạp của tiếng Việt cũng như các tương quan không gian giữa các vùng đặc trưng hình ảnh. Trong nghiên cứu này, đề xuất ViMACSA-GCN, một khung công tác mới cho bài toán MSA tiếng Việt dựa trên mạng nơ-ron tích chập đồ thị. Cụ thể, đặc trưng văn bản và hình ảnh lần lượt được trích xuất bằng PhoBERT và Vision transformer (ViT). Sau đó, các đồ thị đa phương thức được xây dựng để biểu diễn mối quan hệ cấu trúc giữa các thành phần dữ liệu và được tinh chỉnh bằng mạng nơ-ron tích chập đồ thị chuẩn hóa đối xứng. Các biểu diễn đặc trưng được hợp nhất thông qua tầng tuyến tính và sử dụng bộ phân loại để dự đoán ba nhãn tình cảm: Negative, Neutral và Positive. Kết quả thực nghiệm trên tập dữ liệu ViMACSA cho thấy mô hình đạt độ chính xác 87,1 % và F1-score 72,0 %, khẳng định hiệu quả của cách tiếp cận đề xuất đối với MSA tiếng Việt.

title: Label-Kernel Correlation and an Improved Optimization Theory for Neural Networks
abstract: Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) theory oﬀers a principled framework for studying optimization and generalization in over-parameterized neural networks, under constant-kernel, yet it’s convergence theory predictions often present a big gap in the speed of learning observed in practice. This thesis investigates label-Kernel correlation as a unifying quantity that links target structure to kernel geometry and helps explain the theory-practice gap. We pursue two objectives: (i) characterize how label-kernel alignment improves optimization, and (ii) determine the training dynamics of alignment across architectures. On the theoretical side, we develop an improved optimization theory by understanding the interaction between target projections over the eigen directions and eigenvalues. On the experimental side, we track alignment and layer-wise alignment for MLPs, CNNs, and ResNet-18 under SGD-family and adaptive optimizers. We find consistent regimes where SGD-family promote stronger alignment growth in earlier layers with decreasing alignment growth toward later layers, while Adam exhibits more heterogeneous layer-wise patterns. To interpret these trends, we complement alignment with normalized per-layer gradient-of-loss norms and normalized per-layer weight-update energies, which frequently mirror the observed layer-wise alignment trends. Overall, the thesis provides improvement in existing optimization theory for neural networks using label-NTK correlation under constant NTK regime and analyzes the correlation under training in finite width neural networks

title: Decoding AI: Unleashing the Future of Business and Finance
abstract: Decoding AI: Unleashing the Future of Business and Finance examines the transformative impact of Artificial Intelligence on modern business and financial ecosystems. With a strong emphasis on innovation, risk management, ethical deployment, and predictive intelligence, the book offers a comprehensive view of how AI is reshaping sectors such as banking, insurance, accounting, fintech, and beyond.Across twelve insightful chapters, the book traces the evolution of AI-driven transformation, from the emergence of banking in the metaverse and AI-enabled climate risk mitigation to fraud detection, underwriting, credit scoring, and accounting practices, with a special focus on emerging markets such as India. Later chapters explore fintech risk management, cross-sector predictive analytics, and the ethical challenges posed by generative AI. The concluding sections focus on trust, governance frameworks, workforce transformation, and the future trajectory of AI-powered organisations.By blending academic depth with real-world relevance, this book equips readers with strategic, technical, and ethical perspectives needed to navigate AI-led digital transformation.Key Features:Real-world case studies supported by industry data (2019–2024)Covers emerging technologies, including Generative AI and blockchainProvides practical insights into AI-driven risk management and predictive analyticsEthical, regulatory, and governance perspectives for responsible AI adoptionDiscusses applications across finance, healthcare, marketing, and manufacturing

title: XCS for Sequential Perceptual Aliasing in Multi-Step Decision-Making
abstract: Sequential perceptual aliasing is a cognitive challenge for learning agents when robots cannot differentiate states and their associations based on immediate observations, leading to poor decision-making. Existing systems struggle to abstract and distinguish observations effectively to achieve policy learning. This paper addresses this issue by introducing new aliasing types within the context of sequential aliasing and proposing an enhanced XCS classifier system that learns using a complete state-action map. The proposed system called hierarchical Frames-of-References-based XCS (Hi-FoRsXCS), can concatenate sequences of aliased states with the same observation into a chain. Hi- FoRsXCS then predicts associations between the observations and aliased states using the ends of the chain, enabling optimal policy learning with a complete action map. Experimental results demonstrate that Hi-FoRsXCS outperforms the existing systems in terms of accuracy. However, the limitations of Hi-FoRsXCS will be discussed in this paper.

title: Meta-Learning for Rapid Adaptation of TinyML Models on Heterogeneous IoT Sensors
abstract: This research presents a meta-learning framework that is meant to raise the adaptability and cognitive level of TinyML models that are spread over heterogeneous IoT sensor environments to a considerable extent. The performance of conventional TinyML models after deployment is often lower because these models are confronted with new sensor types, data changes, or environmental variability. To get over these problems, the suggested system uses model-agnostic metalearning (MAML) so that the model can “learn how to learn”. The model is not trained only on the fixed tasks, but it is rather prepared to very quickly adjust to a new task with just a few samples. In this way, it is perfectly capable of working in the real-world IoT scenario where data is often limited, noisy, and heterogeneous. This rapid adaptation ability gives the system the freedom to transfer knowledge in an efficient manner across different sensors; thus, the system's reliability and robustness are greatly improved. In order to allow the system to be actually put into use on the edge devices, which have limited resources, the framework employs quantized neural network architectures that can save memory, reduce power consumption, and lower the computational load without losing accuracy. With this optimization, the system can perform real-time inference and also be updated promptly to accommodate the new data and the changed conditions. evidence.title: Meta-Learning for Rapid Adaptation of TinyML Models on Heterogeneous IoT Sensors
evidence.abstract: This research presents a meta-learning framework that is meant to raise the adaptability and cognitive level of TinyML models that are spread over heterogeneous IoT sensor environments to a considerable extent. The performance of conventional TinyML models after deployment is often lower because these models are confronted with new sensor types, data changes, or environmental variability. To get over these problems, the suggested system uses model-agnostic metalearning (MAML) so that the model can “learn how to learn”. The model is not trained only on the fixed tasks, but it is rather prepared to very quickly adjust to a new task with just a few samples. In this way, it is perfectly capable of working in the real-world IoT scenario where data is often limited, noisy, and heterogeneous. This rapid adaptation ability gives the system the freedom to transfer knowledge in an efficient manner across different sensors; thus, the system's reliability and robustness are greatly improved. In order to allow the system to be actually put into use on the edge devices, which have limited resources, the framework employs quantized neural network architectures that can save memory, reduce power consumption, and lower the computational load without losing accuracy. With this optimization, the system can perform real-time inference and also be updated promptly to accommodate the new data and the changed conditions. This kind of continuous learning is a guarantee that IoT applications environmental sensing, for example, or industrial monitoring will be able to rely on the consistency of the performance and its correctness even when the operational contexts are changing.

title: SilentWear: an Ultra-Low Power Wearable System for EMG-based Silent Speech Recognition
abstract: Detecting speech from biosignals is gaining increasing attention due to the potential to develop human-computer interfaces that are noise-robust, privacy-preserving, and scalable for both clinical applications and daily use. However, most existing approaches remain limited by insufficient wearability and the lack of edge-processing capabilities, which are essential for minimally obtrusive, responsive, and private assistive technologies. In this work, we present SilentWear, a fully wearable, textile-based neck interface for EMG signal acquisition and processing. Powered by BioGAP-Ultra, the system enables end-to-end data acquisition from 14 differential channels and on-device speech recognition. SilentWear is coupled with SpeechNet, a lightweight 15k-parameter CNN architecture specifically tailored for EMG-based speech decoding, achieving an average cross-validated accuracy of 84.8pm4.6% and 77.5pm6.6% for vocalized and silent speech, respectively, over eight representative human-machine interaction commands collected over multiple days. We evaluate robustness to repositioning induced by multi-day use. In an inter-session setting, the system achieves average accuracies of 71.1pm8.3% and 59.3\pm2.2% for vocalized and silent speech, respectively. To mitigate performance degradation due to repositioning, we propose an incremental fine-tuning strategy, demonstrating more than 10% accuracy recovery with less than 10 minutes of additional user data. Finally, we demonstrate end-to-end real-time on-device speech recognition on a commercial multi-core microcontroller unit (MCU), achieving an energy consumption of 63.9μJ per inference with a latency of 2.47 ms. With a total power consumption of 20.5mW for acquisition, inference, and wireless transmission of results, SilentWear enables continuous operation for more than 27 hours.
